newsitem.title: GERMANY: Demand for public relations growing - German group.
newsitem.headline: Demand for public relations growing - German group.

text.p: Demand for public relations agencies is growing among companies involved in international business, the German Association of Public Relations Agencies (GPRA) said on Wednesday, reporting on a study it conducted.
A poll of public relations directors at 303 international companies all over the world showed that three-quarters said they required the services of independent agencies for company communications.
The association said in a statement summarising its findings that several market factors had contributed to the public relations boom.
"Not only trends toward corporate expansion and continuous globalisation have been decisive, but also shifts in company structure across industries," the GPRA said.
It said these developments had created a need for better lines of communication outside the corporation.
"The most important tasks of the PR agencies are consumer marketing and media relations," it said.
Among companies surveyed, public relations budgets ranged from 580,000 to several million dollars per year, of which an average of 70 percent went to external public relations firms.

The public relations directors polled worked with an average of four agencies. In 60 percent of cases, agencies take over responsibility for public relations and the average company remains with an agency for eight years.

The GPRA said their efforts to have its 44 agencies certified by the end of the year with the ISO-9001-Norm, an international quality control standard for public relations services, had sparked intense interest across the industry.
